item.title: Yen Falls After BOJ Rate Hike as Oil Extends Slide
item.author: Bloomberg Television
item.content:encoded:
The Bank of Japan raised its benchmark interest rate in a split decision showing dissent within the board. The yen extended its drop against the dollar after BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda gave mixed signals about future rate hikes.
Oil dropped for a third day, with traders looking to the next round of diplomacy that’ll shape the US-Iran war as supply concerns eased. In the Middle East, Saudi Arabia has moved to restore the damaged East-West pipeline to its Red Sea coast, aiming to return about half its capacity within days.
Russia took control of the local businesses of Swiss food giant Nestlé and French supermarket chain Auchan in the Kremlin’s largest takeover of foreign corporate assets since at least 2024 amid rising tensions with Europe.
Today's guests: Carlos Cuerpo, Spanish Minister of Economy, Trade & Enterprise & Deputy Prime Minister; Alessia Berardi, Amundi Investment Institute, Head of Global Macroeconomics and Emerging Markets Strategy; Sayuri Shirai, Keio University Economics Professor & former Bank of Japan Policy Board Member; Martijn Rats, Morgan Stanley, Chief Commodities Strategist --- "The Pulse With Francine Lacqua" is all about conversations with high profile guests in the beating heart of global business, economics, finance and politics. Based in London, we go wherever the story is, bringing you exclusive interviews and market-moving scoops.

item.title: Trump's Low Approval Rating Pressures GOP Ahead of 2026 Midterms
item.author: Bloomberg Television
item.content:encoded:
With the US midterm election about six weeks away, President Donald Trump's approval rating is near record lows. Voters now trust Democrats more than Republicans on a laundry list of issues: to handle the economy, health care, immigration, the deficit, cost of living and foreign wars, according to a fresh New York Times/Siena poll.
"Inflation is still high, consumers are feeling it" and come polling day, voters will be thinking about "affordability, affordability, affordability", says Timothy O'Brien, Senior Executive Editor for Bloomberg Opinion. O'Brien joins "The Pulse with Francine Lacqua" to discuss what's at stake for the Trump administration, and what voters are most concerned about heading into the election. -------- More on Bloomberg Television and Markets

item.title: This Critical Oil Chokepoint Is Now Under Houthi Control | WSJ
item.author: The Wall Street Journal
item.content:encoded:
Iran-backed Houthis have opened a new front in the war in the Middle East. The group’s quick offensive to take the southwestern coast of Yemen and control the Bab al-Mandeb Strait has sent shockwaves around the world.
WSJ explains how the militant group and other Iranian allies have moved to choke off oil shipments and attack Saudi Arabia exports, sending oil prices higher and complicating the U.S. war with Iran.
